rules.rule: Check for urgent anal symptom conditions
rules.problem: Type and trigger are right, but the task is misnamed ('urgent') while most of its items feed non-urgent diagnoses. It does not check for the anal-sex context the proctitis sentence hangs on (Anal penetration), nor for anything that would support the page's other 'likely' diagnoses (tapeworm: flat white segmented worm; anaemia: Hb < 12 woman / < 13 man). Note also that 'Perianal lump' and 'Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum' are not SNOMED descendants of 'Anal finding', so a patient recorded with only one of those will not trigger this task.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable sexually transmitted proctitis from anal symptoms
rules.problem: Or-structure of the three findings is faithful, but the rule omits the 'If patient has anal sex' context in whose bullet the proctitis instruction sits, so probable infective proctitis fires on any painless rectal bleeding, including haemorrhoidal bleeding that the page sends to the Lump/pile column. The page says 'treat for', not 'likely'; probable is defensible as a syndromic working diagnosis but a clinician should confirm the level.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable pinworm from anal itch at night
rules.problem: Type, level ('pinworm likely') and and-structure match the page; the only loss is worm morphology (c015), which SNOMED cannot express.

rules.rule: Urgent: anal symptoms with extremely painful lump or unable to pass stool
rules.problem: Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention'; (and anal (or (and lump severe-pain) does-not-defecate)) mirrors the red box. The 'because of anal symptoms' qualifier on the stool criterion is not expressible and the rule is correspondingly a little broad (c021).

The page has 'Tapeworm likely' when the worm is flat and white with blunt-ended segments (Yes branch of the worm question). This 'X likely' has no rule. (snomed_concept "Infection caused by Taenia" "disorder") exists (also "Cestode infection" "disorder"); the evidence would have to be 'Worms in stool' since morphology has no concept, which would then collide with the pinworm rule, so at minimum a remaining-questions note is needed.

rules.rule: (missing) Diagnose probable anaemia in worm infestation
rules.problem: The worm branch says 'Check Hb. If Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely 44'. This 'X likely' (with a measure task for Hb) is absent. (snomed_concept "Anemia" "disorder") exists; no 'Hemoglobin' observable entity was found in the release, which may be why it was skipped, but the gap should be recorded.

summary: The most consequential problem is the proctitis rule: it drops the 'If patient has anal sex' context that the page's proctitis sentence sits under, so any painless rectal bleeding (typically haemorrhoids) becomes a probable sexually transmitted proctitis. Two 'X likely' diagnoses on the page are missing entirely (tapeworm from a flat, white, segmented worm; anaemia from Hb < 12/13 in the worm branch), and the pinworm rule cannot distinguish worm morphology, so a tapeworm patient with night itch would be called pinworm. The red-box priority rule is structurally faithful but 'Does not defecate' is broader than 'unable to pass stool because of anal symptoms' and will escalate ordinary constipation with any anal finding.
